name: Question 2
problem: Given that  $\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3}+2{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{3}-5{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3},{x}_{4}\in R}$, find a basis for $\text{Null}(A).$
worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Null}(A)$ has the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3}+2{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{3}-5{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3},{x}_{4}\in R.
$$

Expanding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3}+2{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{3}-5{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{4} \\ -5{x}_{4} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore a basis for $\text{Null}(A)$ is

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}
$$

since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$

Question 2
?

Given that Null(A)={[−3x3+2x42x3−5x4x3x4]:x3,x4∈R}, find a basis for Null(A).

a
B={[−3−210],[2501]}
b
B={[3210]}
c
B={[3−201],[−2510]}
d
B={[−1−311]}
e
B={[−3210],[2−501]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Null(A) has the form

[−3x3+2x42x3−5x4x3x4],x3,x4∈R.

Expanding, we get

[−3x3+2x42x3−5x4x3x4]=[−3x32x3x30]+[2x4−5x40x4]=x3[−3210]+x4[2−501].

Therefore a basis for Null(A) is

B={[−3210],[2−501]}

since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate Null(A).
